summary: The submission combines a release-change Control Tower with a question-readiness engine, versioned policy, signed certificates and explicit human review. The source has useful default-deny paths and content-keyed baseline caching. Important boundaries remain incomplete: missing candidate files can disappear from the comparison before selective rerun, baseline-only sample membership can miss newly eligible existing samples, duplicate IDs are normalized away, and review verifies only part of the evidence document. The latter three areas have separately published narrow synthetic corroboration; this reviewer executed no submission code. The missing-candidate-file path is a new source-derived follow-through that still needs an end-to-end positive/negative control. This is a provisional Track 1 review, not an official score, frozen-submission attestation or security/clinical certification.
limitations: Pinned local checkout, not a verified official final-submission receipt; branch names and later changes are outside this pass.
Static source analysis only. No submission code, tests, installers, workflows, notebook, server, hosted endpoint or model was executed.
No sealed envelopes, answer keys or raw clinical datasets were accessed. Numerical correctness, performance, accessibility and fresh-machine setup remain untested.
Source-derived control-flow consequences are labeled as such. Proposed acceptance checks are not observed test results.
The collected text budget is 160 files, 200 KB/file and 4 MB/entry. Complete_with_exclusions is not an exhaustive audit; exclusions and focused follow-ups are recorded.
No official score, cross-team ranking, clinical validity or regulatory/accessibility certification is asserted.

criteria.assessment: Exact profile, label and membership detection is implemented. Duplicate normalization and omitted required candidate inputs need attention. Targeted probes are not recall/false-positive estimates.

findings.title: Missing candidate inputs can bypass analysis availability checks
findings.observation: run_tower builds in_b from files present in the candidate and loads baseline fingerprints only for that set. Files missing from B are listed as not_compared, so the diff never receives the baseline-only file needed to emit file_missing. evaluate_analyses runs the baseline from its full path, but only tries B when a detected relevant change exists. An unchanged carried file plus an omitted required clinical file can therefore leave no relevant change, skip B's analysis and retain the Ready policy fallback when compared baseline hashes verify. A limitation lists the omitted file, but no independent per-analysis candidate-input gate precedes the not_rerun branch. This is a source-derived full-path inference, not an executed Ready result.
findings.impact: The intentional handling of optional omitted RNA should not imply that every candidate file is optional for every analysis. No relevant detected change and inability to compute the protected analysis are different states. A researcher can receive an unaffected explanation for an analysis whose required candidate input was never established as available.
findings.recommendation: Preflight each protected analysis's required inputs in A and B before dependency filtering. Represent omitted optional/unneeded modalities separately from missing required inputs. Preserve the not_compared disclosure, but give an unavailable analysis Insufficient Evidence even if other compared bytes are unchanged. Do not require RNA for an analysis that does not read it.
findings.acceptance_check: With invented complete A and matching public-style expected hashes, compare B containing unchanged protein but no clinical file; verify A1/A2 cannot be labelled unqualified Ready or unaffected. Use valid unchanged A/B as a positive control and omitted RNA with A1/A2 as an optional-modality control. Record the complete run_tower result rather than only diff_releases.
findings.confidence: High for the file-selection and rerun control flow; the stated complete-entry outcome remains unexecuted and requires the named control.

findings.title: Duplicate identifiers disappear before detection
findings.observation: The row loader drops duplicate index values with keep=first before creating the sample list and fingerprints. Numeric and text matrix loaders similarly select the first occurrence of each header ID without retaining duplicate diagnostics. diff_file then compares sets and fingerprints from those normalized views. A parallel invented clinical-row probe reported three input rows reduced to two loaded rows and an empty change list even though the file hash changed. That corroborates the clinical loader/diff case; duplicate matrix headers remain a separate proposed check rather than an executed result here.
findings.impact: Identity ambiguity is removed from the representation the detector inspects. The file hash still identifies changed bytes, so the issue is not a cryptographic hash failure. The missing evidence is a first-class duplicate-ID finding and an explicit policy for which conflicting record, if any, an analysis may use.
findings.recommendation: Validate uniqueness before deduplication and retain occurrence counts, positions and conflicts as evidence. Keep original records intact. If a normalized view is needed for continued diagnostics, label its policy and keep affected analyses unresolved until a person accepts a suitable resolution.
findings.acceptance_check: Append both identical and conflicting repeated clinical IDs with the first record unchanged. Then repeat a matrix sample header, varying the second profile. Require explicit identity diagnostics and separate analysis status. Include unique-ID unchanged inputs as a quiet control.
findings.confidence: High for source and the separately reported clinical fixture; no duplicate-header or end-to-end engine run was performed by this reviewer.

criteria.assessment: Reference-analysis parameters and declared field inspection drive dependency routing; question-readiness specs are separate. Newly eligible existing samples are a concrete impact-map gap, with generic helper corroboration but no event-analysis run by this reviewer.

findings.title: Dependency routing considers baseline members but can miss new entrants
findings.observation: evaluate_analyses takes used from the baseline result's sample_ids and generally requires changed IDs to intersect that set. Only added/new_duplicate changes receive a separate sample-type route. A label change on an existing previously excluded row can alter eligibility without intersecting baseline used, so the candidate result is not run. The separately published invented group-count probe reports baseline n=1, actual changed n=2, but affected=false/not_rerun/after=null. That probe exercises a reviewer-authored analysis, not the actual event A1/A2 functions; this source review traced the generic gate and the corresponding eligibility risk without running it.
findings.impact: A correct impact map must account for records that leave or enter the question's cohort. Checking only previous output membership proves neither candidate membership stability nor that an eligibility-field change is irrelevant. This goes to the Control Tower's central affected-versus-unaffected requirement.
findings.recommendation: Declare eligibility/filter dependencies explicitly and evaluate the relevant candidate population, not only the baseline output IDs. Use the union of before/after potential members or conservatively rerun when an eligibility change cannot be proven irrelevant. Preserve precise reasons for genuinely unrelated changes.
findings.acceptance_check: Start with an existing primary sample excluded for an unknown label, then give it an allowed ER/PAM50 label in B. Demonstrate affected analysis, updated membership and linked evidence; retain an unrelated-field negative control and a still-ineligible label-change case. Verify actual protected analyses in a separately authorized test, not just a generic counting function.
findings.confidence: High for inspected routing and separately reported generic helper reproduction; protected-analysis prevalence and full application behavior are not established.

findings.title: Question review records text without checking its signed spec hash
findings.observation: The engine signs qs.canonical_json through spec_sha256. review_question verifies the certificate and reads verdict/rule IDs from that signed payload, but records question_text from the supplied result.spec without recomputing its canonical hash. The API accepts that client result. The parallel direct-function probe reports an accepted signed review with a changed question string while the certificate remained from the original question. It does not establish that every field or every UI interaction is similarly accepted, and it does not forge a certificate.
findings.impact: A valid signature can be associated with review prose describing a different research question from the one actually evaluated. The official task depends on intended use and cohort definition, so those inputs must remain the subject of the review rather than editable adjacent context.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the original canonical spec from immutable storage, or validate the received canonical spec against the signed spec_sha256 before saving a review. Bind dataset identity, policy and question together and present older reviews as historical when any bound input changes.
findings.acceptance_check: After certification, change question_text, intended use, filters and predictor lists independently. Require rejection or a new evaluation before review. Reordered equivalent JSON keys should remain valid under canonical serialization, and the untouched signed spec should still be reviewable.
findings.confidence: High for the missing verification and separately reported changed-text helper fixture; no browser flow or broader mutation matrix was executed.

findings.title: Baseline cache identity includes current file-content hashes
findings.observation: The release cache key combines a cache-version token with file_sha256 for every selected present file. A same-path content change therefore selects a different cache entry rather than reusing a path-only result. The loader also records both compressed-file and decompressed-content hashes, and the run checks compared baseline file hashes against the frozen checksum map. The verification scope is the selected compared-file set, not a proof of all required candidate inputs or of scientific truth.
findings.impact: This is a useful provenance control and a direct contrast to path-only caches. It helps make cache reuse reproducible and explains why a data hash must be interpreted with its hash_of convention. CFT-01 still needs an independent availability gate.
findings.recommendation: Keep content-bound cache keys and explicit hash conventions. Record the selected-file scope and include required-input availability before judging compatibility. Treat a matching hash as byte identity, not confirmation that an analysis or baseline is scientifically suitable.
findings.acceptance_check: With invented inputs, reuse an unchanged release, replace a file at the same path, and change only compression metadata. Confirm cache and provenance behavior match the declared file/content conventions. Verify omitted required files are still handled by CFT-01's separate gate.
findings.confidence: High for complete cache-key and hash code; no cache read/write or dataset load occurred in this review.

def load_release(path: str | Path, name: str | None = None, include_rna: bool = True,
                 cache_dir: Path | None = None, only: set[str] | None = None) -> Release:
    """Load and fingerprint a release. With cache_dir, a release whose files are byte-identical
    to a previous load (same sha256 per file) is read from the cache instead of re-fingerprinted."""
    import pickle
    path = Path(path)
    if cache_dir is not None:
        present = [f for f in LAYOUT if (path / f).exists() and (include_rna or not f.startswith("rna_"))
                   and (only is None or f in only)]
        key = hashlib.sha256("|".join([CACHE_VERSION] + [f"{f}:{file_sha256(path / f)}" for f in present])
                             .encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
        cached = Path(cache_dir) / f"release-{key}.pkl"
        if cached.exists():
            rel = pickle.loads(cached.read_bytes())
            rel.name, rel.path = name or path.name, path
            for v in rel.files.values():
                v.path = path / v.name
            return rel
        rel = load_release(path, name, include_rna, only=only)
        Path(cache_dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cached.write_bytes(pickle.dumps(rel))

findings.title: Release review checks verdict binding but not the full evidence document
findings.observation: tower_binding contains the question and analysis IDs/verdicts only. Certificate creation uses that binding, while review_release derives required acknowledgments from client-supplied findings and affected_by arrays that are not covered by it. The API passes the supplied findings document directly to the review function. The parallel synthetic probe reports that original Conditional evidence required F1 acknowledgment, but stripping findings/affected_by while retaining the valid certificate allowed a signed approve_with_conditions record with no acknowledgments. The Blocked-verdict guard still rejected approval; no private key was forged and no HTTP/browser exploit was reproduced.
findings.impact: Cryptographic validity establishes exactly what the payload covers, not authenticity of every adjacent field. An evidence-acknowledgment requirement can be reduced through unsigned portions of the submitted document while its verdict remains unchanged. A verified review signature can then describe an incomplete review.
findings.recommendation: Review an immutable server-side result selected by certificate ID, or bind and verify the complete canonical document used for decisions, including findings, analysis evidence, affected_by, repairs and release identity. Reject changed decision inputs before constructing the review. Keep the current signed-verdict restrictions and note requirements.
findings.acceptance_check: Change findings, affected_by, before/after values, repairs and release metadata independently after issuing a certificate. Each changed review request should be rejected or clearly treated as a new unsigned result. The original Conditional result with all required acknowledgments and note is the positive control; Blocked approval must remain rejected.
findings.confidence: High for the partial binding and separately reported direct-function reproduction; no application request or key material was accessed.

findings.title: Policy separates measurements from versioned rules and missing-check states
findings.observation: Policy loads YAML with safe_load and records the rule-file hash. Evaluation produces explicit Insufficient Evidence for missing expected checks, not-evaluable checks and rule references to absent metrics. Conditions use a fixed operator mapping rather than eval. Accepted limitations apply only to allowed Conditional findings, and ignored acceptances remain visible. These paths are useful controls, not a guarantee that all input shapes or metric values are valid.
findings.impact: A reviewer can inspect which measured condition triggered a verdict and distinguish unavailable evidence from an actual negative finding. Constraining accepted limitations prevents an ordinary acceptance list from waiving Blocked findings.
findings.recommendation: Retain the policy/measurement separation, version hash and explicit unavailable states. Keep malformed-input validation separate and test None/type mismatches rather than assuming the generic evaluator covers every shape. Preserve the parallel report's distinct malformed-input findings.
findings.acceptance_check: Omit an expected check, return not_evaluable, remove a referenced metric and submit an unrecognized acceptance. Verify each has a visible and distinct result. Confirm a permitted Conditional acceptance works while Blocked cannot be waived. Do not infer success from source definitions alone.
findings.confidence: High for inspected evaluator controls; no policy tests were run in this pass.

findings.title: Approval policy distinguishes unavailable results and explicit conditions
findings.observation: Allowed decisions depend on the signed verdict. Blocked and Insufficient Evidence allow reject/request_more but no approval; Conditional allows approve_with_conditions. Approval requires the relevant acknowledgments and nontrivial notes under the inspected policy, and release review requires a decision for every supplied analysis. The published Blocked-approval synthetic control was rejected. These are meaningful safeguards even though CFT-04/05 show that surrounding document binding is incomplete. Reviewer names are self-attested strings, not authenticated identity.
findings.impact: The review handoff makes unresolved evidence a separate action rather than equating any recorded interaction with approval. It gives the researcher concrete conditions and a signed record to retain after fixing the evidence-binding boundary.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the decision matrix and original records. Keep the documented end-truncation limitation visible when presenting the hash-chained ledger.
findings.acceptance_check: Exercise each verdict/decision pair with missing versus complete acknowledgments and notes. Retain the rejected Blocked-approval control. def append(event: str, subject: dict) -> dict:
    """Add one entry and return {seq, hash}. Never raises: the ledger must not break a check."""
    try:
        with _lock:
            p = path()
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            last = None
            if p.exists():
                lines = [x for x in p.read_text().splitlines() if x.strip()]
                last = json.loads(lines[-1]) if lines else None
            entry = {"seq": (last["seq"] + 1) if last else 1,
                     "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                     "event": event, "subject": subject,
                     "prev": last["hash"] if last else GENESIS}
            entry["hash"] = _hash(entry)
            entry["sig"] = base64.b64encode(cert._load_key().sign(bytes.fromhex(entry["hash"]))).decode()
            with p.open("a") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
            return {"seq": entry["seq"], "hash": entry["hash"]}
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
        return {"error": f"ledger not written: {e}"}

"""Tamper-evident audit ledger: a hash-chained, signed record of every check and every human decision.

Each entry holds its sequence number, time, event, a short subject (certificate id, verdicts, reviewer),
the previous entry's hash, its own hash, and an Ed25519 signature of that hash. Editing, deleting,
inserting or reordering any past entry breaks the chain, and verify() names the first entry affected.

Limitation: removing entries from the END leaves a valid shorter chain. Record the head hash somewhere
else (the review note, a ticket, an email) to detect that, as Certificate Transparency logs do.
